title: Quantization eval diary — momentum week
body:
Weekly research notes (freeform) — week of 2027-03-02
Owner: Jia Chen; collabs: Marcus, Priya, Ethan
Context: lightweight diary-style capture for quantization/eval/model onboarding experiments. Not a polished PRD.

High-level goals this week:
- Validate int8-ish runtime profile for open-model-X-13B across our serving runtime (nv kernels + kernel-fallback).
- Surface failure modes in evals caused by kv-cache alignment after quantized model restarts.
- Iterate on a small prompt-set (50 exemplars) for conversational quality checks across q4_0 / q8_hybrid variants.

Quick summary of outcomes:
- Throughput: q4 variant (our custom 4-bit mix) shows ~1.9x tokens/sec vs fp16 for 1-request streaming workloads at 4k context on A100s. Latency p50 increased by ~7–12ms in cold start cases (kv warmups as expected).
- Quality: Held steady on instruction-following metrics for short prompts (<128 tokens), but drop in factual recall on longer-chain prompts. Suspect embedding-precision drift in early layers.
- KV-cache: observed misalignment when serving a warm cached session if the model was reloaded with the quantized artifact that changed tokenizer special token mapping (edge case).

Detailed notes / observations:
1) Experiment: open-model-X-13B / q4_mix_v2 on A100s (dedicated).
   - Config: batch_size=1 (streaming), max_new_tokens=512, kv_cache=true, continuous batching off for this run.
   - Observed: sustained throughput 1.9x vs baseline fp16. Memory peak lowered by ~28%.
   - Perf caveat: p99 tail increased when token-dependency graphs triggered attention-kernel fallback (we saw ~150ms tail spikes). Need better kernel selection heuristics.
   - Action: add telemetry tag to kernel-fallback code path (Marcus).

2) Eval: 50-exemplar conv prompt set — blind A/B between fp16 / q4_mix_v2 / q8_hybrid.
   - Metric basket: instruction-compliance (binary), hallucination-rate (manual label), concise-ness (token-length ratio), factual-recall (question-answer accuracy).
   - Results (rough): fp16 compliance 94%, q4 90% (-4), q8 92% (-2). Hallucination rate small increase for q4 on multi-hop questions.
   - Notes: qualitative read-through shows q4 tends to fabricate connectors in long answers. Possible fix: layerwise mixed precision (keep first 2 layers fp16).
   - Action: schedule small run with first-2-layers fp16 + rest q4 (Priya).

3) KV-cache mismatch incident (day 3):
   - Symptoms: when reloading quantized binary after a rolling update, a small subset (~2%) of in-flight sessions returned gibberish tokens until the session was re-initialized.
   - Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer special token ID mapping drift between build artifacts (we changed BOS handling in tokenizer v0.9.7 -> v0.9.8) combined with cached kv sequences referencing absolute positions.
   - Quick mitigation: pin tokenizer version at model artifact level; add startup assertion to verify special token IDs vs expected signature.
   - Action items: Jia to open PR to artifact builder to emit tokenizer_signature.json; Ethan to add runtime assert + graceful fallback to re-tokenize session if mismatch.

4) Onboarding checklist hits / friction:
   - Model tarball vs containerized artifact: our onboarding script assumes tokenizer at /opt/model/tokenizer.json; some external artifacts put it in /model/tokenizer. We need canonical layout.
   - Suggestion: enforce a manifest.json field (tokenizer_path + tokenizer_signature) and fail fast in onboarding if missing.
   - Action: Marcus to update onboarding script; add to checklist docs (CONFLUENCE-ML-1024).

5) Small probe: micro-batching impact on quantized runs
   - Setup: batch_size 4 vs batch_size 1 on identical hardware for q4_mix_v2.
   - Result: batching increases overall throughput but hurts p50 for single-request latency by ~15–30ms (tradeoff obvious). For our user-facing streaming use-case, prefer single-request pipelines with aggressive batching disabled. For backend high-throughput routes (embeddings/async) use batching enabled.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the observed factual degradation due to quantization-induced representational loss, or due to tokenizer/layout differences? Need ablation: quantize with original tokenizer artifact vs quantize after tokenization changes. (Jia to run)
- How to better detect early kernel-fallbacks and route low-latency traffic away from nodes that historically trigger fallbacks? Can we encode a node-level score in the routing table?
- Should we expand the prompt-set to 200 exemplars to reduce sampling noise? Pros: better statistical power. Cons: eval cost / runtime. Proposed: incremental add 25/week.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: add telemetry tag to kernel-fallback path; update onboarding script manifest requirement. (ETA 2027-03-11)
- Priya: run mixed-precision ablation (first-2-layers fp16 + q4 rest) on 50-ex exemplar set; capture hallucination statistics. (ETA 2027-03-10)
- Jia: run tokenizer-stable quantization ablation (quantize model with pinned tokenizer v0.9.7 artifact) and report. (ETA 2027-03-09)
- Ethan: runtime assert + auto-retokenize fallbacks for KV-cache mismatch; write small test harness to reproduce. (ETA 2027-03-12)
- All: sync Friday 30m async notes in #applied-ml-quant (short pulse check).

Quick links / cross-references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-playbooks/pull/142 (artifact manifest prototype)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ML-1024 (onboarding checklist draft)
- Jira: JIRA-ML-2387 (kv-cache mismatch incident)

Notes to self / random scribbles:
- Consider adding a micro-benchmark ci job that runs a 10-sample streaming latency test post-artifact-publish (cheap guardrail).
- Think about a "tokenizer signature" binary hash embedded in model weights to detect drift earlier.
- We should capture exact prompt anchors that trigger hallucinations and surface them as small unit tests in eval harness.

Meeting cadence:
- Weekly sync Fridays 11:00 (30m) — short standup + 2 demos max.
- Deep-dive every 3 weeks for longer roadblocks.

End of diary entry.

-- Jia
